name: Amikacin
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Amikacin is an aminoglycoside excreted almost entirely unchanged by the kidneys; it is nephrotoxic and ototoxic (boxed warning), with higher risk in kidney impairment, high doses and long courses. The US label adjusts by serum creatinine or creatinine clearance, either by lengthening the interval (serum creatinine × 9 hours) or by reducing the dose, with serum-level monitoring. It does not give a dialysis dose. Hemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis remove it.
kidney_function_basis: Label uses serum creatinine (interval = SCr × 9 h) or creatinine clearance (proportional reduction); no fixed bands.

bands.recommendation: Normal kidney function: 15 mg/kg/day in 2 or 3 equal doses (7.5 mg/kg every 12 hours or 5 mg/kg every 8 hours); maximum 1.5 g/day; 7 to 10 days usual (label). If serum creatinine is raised, adjust as below. Monitor levels.

Give the normal 7.5 mg/kg loading dose, then either extend the interval (hours = serum creatinine in mg/dL × 9) or, at fixed 12-hour intervals, reduce the dose in proportion to CrCl (or divide the normal dose by serum creatinine) (label). Measure peaks and troughs: avoid peak above 35 mcg/mL and trough above 10 mcg/mL.

Measure peaks and troughs: avoid peak above 35 mcg/mL and trough above 10 mcg/mL.

Give the normal 7.5 mg/kg loading dose, then either extend the interval (hours = serum creatinine in mg/dL × 9) or, at fixed 12-hour intervals, reduce the dose in proportion to CrCl (or divide the normal dose by serum creatinine) (label). Measure peaks and troughs: avoid peak above 35 mcg/mL and trough above 10 mcg/mL. Toxicity risk is highest here; specialist input.

hd.text: The label's kidney methods should not be used during dialysis and no dialysis dose is given; hemodialysis removes amikacin (label). Dose by serum levels after dialysis with specialist input.

pd.text: No PD dose in label; peritoneal dialysis removes amikacin. For PD-associated peritonitis (ISPD 2022): 2 mg/kg intraperitoneally once daily, intermittent (in one exchange daily with a dwell of at least 6 hours); continuous dosing is not advised. Specialist input.

crrt.text: Li 2020 (CRRT review): first dose of at least 25 mg/kg for target peaks in CVVHDF; 25 mg/kg every 48 hours with therapeutic drug monitoring in CVVH or CVVHDF (30 mL/kg/h). CVVHD: no accurate regimen; individualize from first-dose levels.

dialyzable: Yes: hemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis remove amikacin (label 10). Protein binding 0% to 11%.
monitoring: Peak (30 to 90 minutes after dose) and trough levels; serum creatinine or CrCl before and during therapy; urinalysis; audiometry and vestibular function, especially with kidney impairment or courses over 10 days. Avoid other nephrotoxic or ototoxic drugs and potent diuretics.

pediatric.approved_ages: Children and older infants; newborns with caution (label).
pediatric.usual_dose: Children and older infants with normal kidney function: 15 mg/kg/day in 2 or 3 doses. Newborns: 10 mg/kg loading dose, then 7.5 mg/kg every 12 hours (label).
pediatric.neonates: 10 mg/kg loading dose, then 7.5 mg/kg every 12 hours; half-life longer in premature and neonatal infants (renal immaturity; label).

renal.recommendation: Usual 15 mg/kg/day in 2 or 3 doses; TDM (label).
Label kidney methods (interval = serum creatinine × 9 h, or proportional dose reduction) are not age-limited; monitor levels.

pd.text: No label dose; see ISPD 2022; specialist.

crrt.text: No pediatric CRRT data in the cited sources; level-guided; specialist.

adult: Label describes conventional multiple-daily dosing; extended-interval (once-daily) dosing is not in the label.
ISPD 2022 intraperitoneal amikacin dose not stated: full text not accessible in PMC this session. Dr. Rivero to supply or approve the guideline numbers.
HD gray because no dose is given; 'dose after dialysis by levels' is clinical practice, not label text.
pediatric: The serum creatinine × 9 rule was derived in adults; applying it to children (whose creatinine is lower) is the label's general wording, not a pediatric study.

revision_log.change: PD tile: ISPD 2022 Table 5 IP dose for PD-associated peritonitis, 2 mg/kg IP daily intermittent (one exchange, dwell ≥6 h); continuous not advised.
